title: Yes/no questions, short answers, meeldima and oskama + da-infinitive
explanation:
A yes/no question starts with Kas: Kas sa oled eestlane?
Short answers repeat the verb, not just 'yes/no'. Jah, ... küll = yes; Ei, ei ... = no. In the negative the verb loses its personal ending (ei + stem).
QuestionYesNo
Kas sa oled ...?Jah, olen küll.Ei, ei ole.
Kas sul on ...?Jah, on küll.Ei, ei ole.
Kas sa räägid ...?Jah, räägin küll.Ei, ei räägi.
Kas sa oskad ...?Jah, oskan küll.Ei, ei oska.
Kas sulle meeldib ...?Jah, meeldib küll.Ei, ei meeldi.
Mulle meeldib (I like) and ma oskan (I can / know how) are followed by the da-infinitive (the second dictionary form): Mulle meeldib ujuda. Ma oskan laulda. With languages, oskama and rääkima take the partitive: Ma oskan eesti keelt.

title: Imperative: commands to one person (sina) and to several / polite (teie)
explanation:
To one person (sina): take the 1st person present (ma-form) and drop -n: kordan → Korda!, ütlen → Ütle!, loen → Loe!
To several people or politely (teie): take the da-infinitive and replace -da with -ge or -ta with -ke: kirjutada → Kirjutage!, korrata → Korrake!. After l, n, r the ending is -ge: tulla → Tulge!, minna → Minge!

title: Ordinal numbers 1–10 and 'Mitmendal korrusel?' (on which floor)
explanation:
Mitmes? = which one (in order). The answer is an ordinal in the nominative: See on kolmas korrus.
Mitmendal? = on which one. Take the genitive (II form) of the ordinal and add -l; the noun takes -l too: Ma elan kolmandal korrusel.

explanation:
To say where something is, take the genitive (II form) and add -s ('in', inside) or -l ('on', at, open places).

title: Three forms of nouns; partitive after numbers and after 'ei ole'
explanation:
Every noun has three key forms: I nominative (Mis? Kes?), II genitive (Mille? Kelle?), III partitive (Mida? Keda?).
Use the partitive (III): after numbers 2 and above (kaks voodit) and in the negative Mul ei ole ... (Mul ei ole tolmuimejat). After üks the noun stays nominative: üks voodi.

vaipvaibakaks vaipa
tolmuimejatolmuimejakaks tolmuimejat
Note the 'weak/strong' change: often II is short and III is long (kapp – kapi – kappi; laud – laua – lauda).

title: Comparative (-m) and superlative (kõige + -m)
explanation:
Comparative = genitive (II form) + -m: sõbralik → sõbraliku → sõbralikum (friendlier). 'than' = kui.
Superlative = kõige + comparative: kõige sõbralikum (the friendliest).

Estonian has no verb 'to have': it says 'at me is': Mul on koer. In the negative the thing goes into the partitive: Mul ei ole kassi.

I form (nominative): Mul on üks vend. Minu vend on arst.
II form (genitive) = 'of', before another noun: Minu venna nimi on Leo. (my brother's name)
